name: Box64 dynarec: self-modifying-code detection needs a 4096-byte host page, because it mprotects individual guest pages
component: Box64: protectDB / protectDBJumpTable + FillBlock exec-protection check
required_postconditions: a single 4 KiB x86-64 guest page can be write-protected without affecting neighbouring guest pages
PROT_EXEC on the host reflects the guest's own exec permission at 4 KiB granularity, so req_prot can include PROT_EXEC
when box64_pagesize > 4096 both properties are lost: a host page holding both code and data cannot be write-protected, and the block is tagged PROT_NEVERCLEAN so every entry re-tests the code instead

failure_sink.description: there is no failure: the code silently takes a different correctness model. With a >4K page it logs 'mixed code+data host page %p, using always_test instead of mprotect' at LOG_INFO and sets PROT_NEVERCLEAN, and FillBlock stops requiring PROT_EXEC at all (req_prot becomes PROT_READ). The dirty-code guarantee is traded for a re-test on every entry.

source_locations.symbol: identical req_prot expression on the block-lookup path
if(box64_pagesize>4096) prot = getProtection_fast(addr); // re-read because protectDB may have added NEVERCLEAN
if(!box64_pagesize) box64_pagesize = 4096; // 4096 is also the fallback when sysconf fails

extraction_limitations: box64_pagesize is a runtime value from sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE), not a compile-time constant; the 4096 modelled here is the value the fast path is conditioned on, taken from the equality test itself.

x_campaign.rationale: The probe measured page_size 4096 on this x86-64 Linux host, which is exactly the value the fast path requires; this contract is the one that should flip to UNSUPPORTED on a 16K Apple Silicon or 64K ARM host.
